# Chapter 1: Morning at the Pier

Dawn crept quietly across the wooden planks of the old harbor, where *gentle waves* tapped against the hulls of moored fishing boats. Saleem stood near the edge of the pier, watching the crews return after a long night at sea[^1].

He pulled a small salt-stained notebook from his coat pocket and opened it to a page written in **steady, deliberate** ink ten years earlier. The notebook was never a simple diary; it was a quiet map of everything his father had left behind.

## The Corner Tea House

Inside the tea house overlooking the bay, old Mahmoud poured hot tea into small glass cups and glanced toward the horizon.

***

An hour passed before the clouds parted and sunlight scattered across the water in bright golden threads.

> To Saleem,
> If these lines reach you one day, remember that the northern lighthouse guided more than ships; it kept our ledger safe beneath the stone stairs.

# Chapter 2: The Coastal Path

Saleem followed the narrow rocky trail winding between coastal hills and deep blue water. Sea breeze carried the scent of kelp and the cries of gulls circling high above the cliffs.

[^1]: The eastern pier served local fishing boats since the late nineteenth century.
